region: Union Springs · Cayuga Lake, Finger Lakes, New York
about: When Tom and Susan Higgins set out to make Pinot Noir in the Finger Lakes, Tom spent years reading geological maps for one thing: limestone. They found it on a slope a few hundred feet from Cayuga Lake’s eastern shore near Union Springs, bought the land in 2007 and planted seven Pinot Noir clones in 2010. Their first estate harvest came in 2012. Heart & Hands has since become one of the region’s most closely watched Pinot Noir specialists, in a part of New York better known for Riesling.

The estate sits on the Onondaga limestone formation, with a pocket of harder dolomite in the middle Pinot Noir block; the winery compares the two stones to the limestones under Burgundy’s Côte de Nuits. Each vineyard lot is fermented and aged apart, and the best are bottled as single-vineyard Estate wines such as this one. The grapes are hand-picked at dawn and berry-sorted, then fermented for about two weeks in small open-top vats, punched down by hand twice a day, and moved by gravity into François Frères French oak barrels.

2021 was a challenging year in the vineyard, with higher disease pressure that demanded careful leaf pulling for airflow, heavy late-summer rain followed by a dry, sunny September that let the grapes ripen. The winery’s note describes red raspberry, red cherry and light spice, a balance of acidity and tannin, and a finish of vanilla, minerals, spice and earth.
